title: The Tom Powell Drum and Bugle Corps
summary: Terry plays bugle in the 1935 drum and bugle corps and builds embouchure skills without valves.

bands.name: Tom Powell Drum and Bugle Corps

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: I think that was on the other tape, so do that story.

In 1935, we – I was with an organization. At this point I’m living with my older sister, Ada and Sy, on 2913 Lawton, and the Tom Powell Drum and Bugle Corps convened on Vandervan and Finney, which is 3900 West and about 10 blocks the other way, so I had to walk 20 or so blocks to this rehearsal for the Tom Powell Drum and Bugle Corps, and I was assigned a bugle. So at least – I don’t have valves at this point, but at least I’ve got all the manipulation, articulation, and the embouchure functions down perfect. [Terry vocalizes and up and down buzzing sound.] That’s one of the things we assign the kids today, is to learn to use the embouchure at the point where you just imagine you don’t even have valves. [Terry plays a buzzing melody with his lips alone.] And then when you put it together with the fingering, it’s a lot easier. So I had a chance to do a lot of that on a bugle. [Terry vocalizes Reveille and another melody.] - that kind of stuff, all of which I tried to figure out ways and means of encompassing that into jazz, and some of the systems that we use in teaching are built on some of those theories that we concocted back in those days, which worked good.
